newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end lower, Colbun plunges.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end lower, Colbun plunges.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed softer in volatile trade with the top losers, including state power utility Colbun Machicura, reacting to the government's rejection of bids from potential "strategic partners" for the utility, traders said.
The market is seen resuming its downward drift at the opening with institutional investors staying on the sidelines, they said.
The 40-share IPSA index was off 0.43 percent at 101.25 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.39 percent to 5,522.73 points amid turnover of nearly 11 billion pesos.
Traders noted that most of the volume came from dealers trading their own portfolios.
Utility Colbun plunged 10 percent in heavy dealing on news the government failed to sell a 37.5 percent stake in the firm to a private investor.
"The stock has been rising in recent days as people thought the sale price would be close to 60 pesos a share," said one trader.
Colbun closed down 10.1 percent at 46.75 pesos.
Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts closed broadly lower with other power shares among the leading losers.
Electricity stocks have been unsettled by uncertainty over how far the government will cut distribution and generation tariffs in its November review, traders said.
Analysts expect generating prices to fall by eight percent and distribution tariffs by up to 10 percent.
The new tariffs will take into account lower operating costs as the result of the supply of natural gas from Argentina which will begin next year.
Chilgener dropped 1.19 percent at 2,490 pesos with Enersis off 0.78 percent at 254 pesos.
